challenges.name: put-patch-merge-quiz
challenges.title: Replace or change: what did the request do to the course?
challenges.description: Two requests against course crs_42: the save from admin app 2.3 that started the incident, and a JSON merge patch sent by the new course editor.

questions.explanation: True. RFC 9110 defines PUT as replacing the state of the target resource with the state in the request body, so a member the body does not contain is not kept: the server reset prerequisites and certificate to their defaults because admin app 2.3 has never heard of them. A JSON merge patch (RFC 7396) works the other way round: members absent from the patch are left unchanged, so a patch with only the new title changes only the title. The misconception is that PUT means "update whatever I send"; that is what PATCH with a merge patch means, and it is why edits from forms that an older client builds belong in PATCH.

questions.question:
Before: GET /courses/crs_42 returned
{"id":"crs_42","title":"HTTP Fundamentals","tags":["http","api"],"discountPrice":99000}

The new course editor sent:
PATCH /courses/crs_42
Content-Type: application/merge-patch+json

{"tags":["http"],"discountPrice":null}

The server applies the patch with the RFC 7396 algorithm and answers 200 OK.

Statement: "After this request the course still has the tag \"api\", because a merge patch only adds or replaces the array elements it lists, and discountPrice is still 99000, because null members in a merge patch are skipped."
questions.explanation: False, on both counts. RFC 7396 merges objects member by member, but any value that is not an object, arrays included, simply replaces the current value: tags becomes ["http"] and the tag "api" is gone. A member set to null in a merge patch removes that member, so discountPrice is removed (or reset to its default if the schema requires it). The misconception is to read a merge patch as "merge everything": it merges objects only, and null is an instruction, not a placeholder. To add one tag or to set a value to null you need JSON Patch (RFC 6902) or a dedicated endpoint.
